summary: In ansible-core 2.12 INTERPRETER_PYTHON defaults to auto and the fallback list prefers Python 3, so remote hosts quietly use Python 3 over Python 2; the fallback list can be changed with ansible_interpreter_python_fallback.
questions: Why did Ansible start using python3 on my hosts instead of /usr/bin/python?
How do I change the list of Python interpreters Ansible tries?
What is the default interpreter_python setting now?

answer_card.title: Python interpreter discovery defaults to auto
answer_card.answer_md:
`INTERPRETER_PYTHON` defaults to **`auto`** and `INTERPRETER_PYTHON_FALLBACK` prefers **Python 3**, so Python 3 is used quietly when available. To force an interpreter set `ansible_python_interpreter`; to change the search order set **`ansible_interpreter_python_fallback`**:

```yaml
ansible_interpreter_python_fallback: ['/usr/bin/python3.11', '/usr/bin/python3']
```
